data.long_meaning: Parbhakar is a Sanskrit name derived from the word 'Parabhava', which means 'supreme existence' or 'supreme creator'. This name is often used to honor the divine power and creator of the universe. The name Parbhakar carries the meaning “Supreme Creator” and is chosen by families in Hindu traditions for the positive qualities it expresses. Linguistically it belongs to the Sanskrit tradition and is also used in Hindi, Sanskrit, Marathi. Parents who choose Parbhakar usually hope their child will grow to embody supreme creator and live with faith, good character and purpose.

historical_references.reference: Parbhakar was a powerful Chalukya king who ruled over the southern Indian region of Vijayanagara in the 13th century.
historical_references.context: The Chalukya dynasty was a major power in the Deccan region of India from the 6th to the 13th century. Parbhakar is known to have expanded the kingdom's territories and is considered to be one of the strongest rulers of the later Chalukya period.

historical_references.reference: Historical records show that Parbhakar was a Jaina monk and philosopher who lived in the 5th or 6th century. The name Parbhakar carried significant spiritual weight in that era.
historical_references.context: Parbhakar is known for his contributions to Jaina philosophy, particularly in the areas of epistemology and metaphysics. He wrote several commentaries on Jaina texts and is considered to be an influential figure in Jaina intellectual history.
